Source: On pelvic examination, the vagina is dry and atrophic with a 2-cm tender, palpable anterior vaginal mass.
A 52-year-old G3P3 woman presents to clinic with a 2-year history of urinary incontinence.
She does not endorse any loss of urine with coughing or laughter.
She has been treated for 2 urinary tract infections over the past 6 months.
She has had frequent, involuntary loss of urine over the last 2 years but presented today because of 10 days of dysuria.
The mass does not change with Valsava maneuver.
Her postvoid residual volume is 60 mL.
She has no chronic medical illnesses and no surgical history.
Her temperature is 99.5°F (37.5°C), blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg, pulse is 92/min, and respirations are 15/min.
